claims.claim: Go would give you far lower memory per connection [than Reverb]
claims.about: Go WebSocket server vs Laravel Reverb (PHP)
claims.measured: Not measured. Closest figures are HTTP peak memory in the 256-connection I/O-wait test: go-gin 16 MB, go-nethttp 15 MB, php-laravel 62 MB, php-laravel-octane 116 MB
claims.why: The benchmark does not include Reverb or any WebSocket workload and does not measure memory per connection. Its HTTP figures only loosely suggest that Go uses less memory than Laravel.

claims.claim: Without ext-uv or ext-ev, PHP falls back to stream_select, which has a hard ~1,024 file-descriptor limit and is slower
claims.about: PHP event loop used by Reverb
claims.why: None of the measured servers is a PHP event-loop server, and nothing compares event-loop backends or file-descriptor limits.

claims.claim: Many teams run well past 60,000 chats on PHP-based WebSocket servers once configured properly
claims.why: The benchmark measures HTTP request throughput only, not how many WebSocket connections a server can hold at once.

claims.claim: Centrifugo is mature and built for very high connection counts
claims.why: Centrifugo was not benchmarked, and connection capacity was not measured for any server.
